projectBackground.name: Hydraulic Press Frame Redesign
projectBackground.context: A field failure cracked a bolt on a press frame. The design must be re-verified before production resumes.

manager.name: Hyun-woo Choi
manager.note: Show the load, the area, the stress and the margin. If the safety factor is below target, say so and fix it.

assignment.title: Re-verify the press frame design
assignment.brief: Calculate stress and safety factor, check a pressure vessel, verify three joints in Excel and write the design justification.

documents.name: Load Case
documents.note: Bolt load 50 kN on an area of 400 mm²; yield strength 250 MPa.

documents.name: Vessel Data
documents.note: Internal pressure 2 MPa; radius 500 mm; wall thickness 10 mm.

documents.name: Joint Schedule
documents.note: Three joints with loads and tensile areas.

tasks.title: Bolt Stress
tasks.prompt: A 50 kN load acts on an area of 400 mm². What is the stress (MPa)?
tasks.mistake: Using kN with mm² gives a number 1,000x too small.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Factor of Safety
tasks.prompt: Yield strength is 250 MPa and working stress is 125 MPa. What is the factor of safety?
tasks.reasoning: Safety factor is capacity over demand.
tasks.mistake: Quoting stress alone says nothing about margin.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Hoop Stress
tasks.prompt: A thin-walled vessel: pressure 2 MPa, radius 500 mm, thickness 10 mm. Hoop stress = P x r / t. What is it (MPa)?
tasks.mistake: Using diameter instead of radius doubles the result.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Fatigue
tasks.prompt: A bolt that sees millions of load cycles at stress below yield cracked. What is the likely cause?
tasks.reasoning: Cyclic loads can cause failure below yield.
tasks.tip: Check fatigue for rotating or cyclic parts.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Joint Verification (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Stress (D = B x 1000 / C, MPa) and factor of safety (E = 250 / D) for each joint. Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: J3's safety factor is below 1 — it will yield.
tasks.tip: Flag any joint under the target factor.
tasks.mistake: Averaging safety factors hides the failing joint.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Design Justification
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence justification of the redesign.
tasks.modelAnswer: Joint J3 carries 45 kN on only 150 mm², giving 300 MPa against a 250 MPa yield (safety factor 0.83), which explains the field failure. I propose increasing the bolt size to raise the area to at least 400 mm², giving stress of about 112 MPa and a safety factor above 2. The cyclic load requires a fatigue check, so I recommend rolled threads and a pre-load specification. The vessel hoop stress of 100 MPa is within allowable limits.
tasks.reasoning: A good justification names the root cause, the corrective change and the check.
tasks.mistake: Replacing a bolt without calculation repeats the failure.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Undersized Bolt
caseStudy.background: A press frame used bolts sized by 'what we used last time'. Under cyclic load they fatigued and a frame cracked, stopping the line for three weeks.
caseStudy.challenges: No calculation was required for 'repeat' designs.
caseStudy.solution: Atlas introduced a mandatory calculation check for every load-bearing joint.
